chunks.arabic_text: وَ رَوَى مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْوَلِيدِ عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ الْجُعْفِيِّ قَالَ

translations.en: Muhammad ibn al-Walid narrated from Hammad ibn ʿUthman, from Ismaʿil al-Juʿfi, who said:

chunks.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ يَقُولُ: «الْجَدُّ يُقَاسِمُ الْإِخْوَةَ وَ لَوْ كَانُوا مِائَةَ أَلْفٍ».

translations.en: I heard Abu Jaʿfar عليه السلام say: "The grandfather shares the inheritance with the siblings, even if they were one hundred thousand."

en.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling in inheritance: the grandfather shares in the estate together with the siblings of the deceased. The ruling applies regardless of how numerous the siblings may be, emphasizing the grandfather’s recognized inheritance position in this case.
en.seo_question: Does the grandfather inherit together with the siblings in Shia inheritance law?

key_terms.الْجَدُّ: the grandfather as a legal heir in inheritance
key_terms.يُقَاسِمُ: shares jointly in the inheritance portion
key_terms.الْإِخْوَةَ: the siblings who inherit alongside another heir
key_terms.مِائَةَ أَلْفٍ: a hyperbolic expression showing that large numbers do not change the ruling
